title: Apprentice to Senior — Transition Evidence Roadmap
content:
Purpose: Lightweight, evidence-first playbook to guide internal apprenticeship promotions into senior IC roles. Designed for managers, mentors, and HR partners who need a repeatable, low-friction way to collect signals, run lightweight calibration interviews, and onboard newly promoted engineers through their first 90 days as a senior.

Context and constraints:
- Target audience: internal apprentices (6–18 month programs), mentors, hiring managers, people ops.
- Goal: turn ad-hoc promotion calls into documented, comparable evidence sets so decisions are defensible and promotable employees have a clear runbook for success after promotion.
- Assumption: candidate already passed a baseline skills assessment during apprenticeship; this focuses on senior-level competencies (autonomy, cross-team influence, technical ownership).

High-level flow (compact):
1) Evidence collection window (2 weeks): mentee compiles artifacts; mentor and manager add commentary.
2) Calibration + assessment interview (1 hour): peer/hiring-manager panel using the rubric below.
3) Decision checkpoint (People Ops + Manager): accept / request development plan / decline.
4) Promotion kickoff & first-90 onboarding plan: checklist and mentor pairing.

Artifacts to collect (minimum required):
- 3 impact writeups (200–400 words each) that follow the STAR format: situation, task, action, result. At least one should show independent ownership.
- PR/merge history: 5 representative PRs with short notes on complexity and ownership.
- Design doc or architecture notes: one doc where the apprentice led or substantially co-authored changes.
- Feedback snapshots: at least two peer feedback notes (Slack threads, review comments, 1:1 highlights).
- Oncall runbook incident summary: if applicable, a brief incident postmortem where the apprentice contributed to RCA or mitigation.
- Mentorship log: one page summary of mentee-as-mentor evidence if they have coached others (shadow sessions, code reviews).

Optional but encouraged artifacts:
- Customer/partner kudos, data showing latency/cost improvements, test coverage increase, performance benchmarks.
- Mini-roadmap they owned for a quarter (OKR-style bullets).

Rubric (panel-driven, use numeric scoring 1–5, then narrative):
Scale: 1 = not yet, 2 = developing, 3 = meets expectations for senior, 4 = strong senior, 5 = exceptional (ready to mentor other seniors).
Competency areas (panel scores each):
- Technical Ownership: defines system boundaries, makes tradeoffs, leads rollouts.
- Architecture & Design: designs for scale, clear documentation and tradeoff reasoning.
- Delivery & Execution: predictable delivery, decomposition, risk management.
- Cross-team Influence: communicates and negotiates across teams, drives alignment.
- Mentorship & Talent Development: grows others, gives constructive reviews, delegates.
- Reliability & Operability: anticipates production issues, improves observability/exec paths.
- Communication & Stakeholder Management: concise written updates, effective syncs.

Minimum promotion gating logic (example):
- At least four competency scores >= 3, with none below 2.
- Technical Ownership >= 3 required.
- All three required artifacts submitted and verified.
- Manager + mentor written support statement.

Panel interview template (60 minutes):
- 0–5 min: quick framing + role expectations from manager
- 5–20 min: candidate walkthrough of one impact writeup (deep dive: decisions and tradeoffs)
- 20–35 min: design/architecture scenario (situation provided in advance; 10–15 min discussion)
- 35–45 min: behavioral probes focused on cross-team influence and mentorship
- 45–55 min: clarifying Qs from panel, ask the candidate to summarize top 2 priorities in first 90 days as senior
- 55–60 min: panel scoring and calibration notes captured by panel lead

Manager + mentor support statement (short template):
- Manager: campus to senior checklist — one paragraph describing why promotion is right now, key evidence, risk areas to watch, suggested 30/60/90 goals.
- Mentor: one paragraph about technical growth, communication growth, recommended shadowing pairings after promotion.

Post-promotion 90-day onboarding checklist (for promoted apprentices):
- Day 0–7: promotion announcement, title update, systems access, 1:1 kickoff with new skip-level, confirm mentor pairing.
- Week 1–4: shadow higher-level planning meetings (1 per week), pair on a medium-impact ticket, establish new ownership of a service or component.
- Week 4–8: run a small cross-team change with mentor as observer, present a short architecture review to peers.
- Week 8–12: lead a retrospective on the cross-team change, record a 10-minute tech talk for the team.
- End of 90: 30-minute promotion retrospective with manager + mentor, update evidence ledger.

Quick templates to paste into artifacts: 
- Impact writeup header: "Title / Project: 
Role: 
Timeline: 
Stakeholders: 
Problem: 
My actions (bullets): 
Outcome (metrics / customer quotes): 
What I learned / follow-ups:"

- Manager support stub: "I support promotion: [yes/no/conditional]. Top reasons: [3 bullets]. Risk watch: [1–2 bullets]. 30/60/90 priority bullets:"

- Mentor note stub: "Observed growth areas: [3 bullets]. Coaching plan for next 90 days: [3 bullets]. Recommended pairing: [names]."

Common risks & mitigation guidance for People Ops:
- Sparse artifact set: return to manager with 1-week extension request and a targeted list of missing artifacts.
- Single-person bias: ensure at least one panelist is from outside the direct squad.
- Over-index on tenure: require evidence of independent ownership rather than time served.
- Onboarding gap after promotion: mandate an explicit 90-day plan and re-check at 45 days.

Calibration deck pointers (for People Ops running the decision meeting):
- Slide 1: Snapshot of candidate (tenure, program length, key systems).
- Slide 2: Summary of artifacts and top 3 impact bullets.
- Slide 3: Rubric table (scores + short rationales).
- Slide 4: Manager & mentor statements.
- Slide 5: Recommended outcome + onboarding plan.

Small experiments to pilot with this playbook (notes):
- Pilot group: 6 apprentices across infra and serving-runtime teams for Q4.
- Measure: percentage promoted, 45-day retention of new responsibilities, manager satisfaction (survey).
- Feedback loop: collect panelist notes in a shared Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-APPT-4432) and iterate rubric weights after first cycle.

In-doc checklist for the apprentice (copy this into their evidence packet):
- [ ] 3 STAR impact writeups uploaded
- [ ] 5 representative PRs flagged with owner notes
- [ ] Design doc linked + short summary
- [ ] Mentor log appended
- [ ] Manager support stub filled
- [ ] Panel interview scheduled

Notes to reviewers (tone & expectations):
- Keep feedback evidence-driven: cite artifacts and timestamps where possible.
- Use the numeric rubric to anchor, but write short rationale phrases to help calibration.
- If recommending "conditional promotion", specify exact deliverables and timeframe (eg: "reach 3/5 in Cross-team Influence in 60 days by leading X project").

Last bits: where to store artifacts
- Primary folder: Drive -> shared_drives/company/misc/promotions/apprentice-to-senior/<candidate-name> (People Ops will create after nomination).
- Copy of panel notes -> Confluence page ID in linked_artifacts.

Open questions for the pilot (to discuss with people ops lead):
- Should we require at least one external reviewer for all promotions, or only when manager/mentor disagree?
- How strict should scoring thresholds be for disciplines like Reliability vs Mentorship?

End of doc — lightweight, meant to be pasted into Drive as a working doc and updated as the pilot runs.
